# The KK norm functor, part 3: the Tate diagonal and the non-nuclear adversarial test

Lane ex2-uct-norm-functor, 2026-09-13.  Unreviewed.  Continues parts 1–2.
Notation: `G = Z/p = <σ>`, `N` the norm functor, `1_T = cone(P → C)` the Tate
object of part 2, §8, and `T(A) = 1_T ⊗ N(A)`.  For `Res E ≃ 0`,
`e_E = (1 + θ_E + ⋯ + θ_E^(p−1))/p` is the central idempotent of
`zp-restriction-trivial-splits-cellular-plus-phantom`, and `(1 − e)E` is the
phantom part.

## 9. Phantom transfer

**Lemma 1.**  `θ_(1_T) = 1`.

*Proof.*  `P` lies in the localizing subcategory generated by the induced
objects `Ind_1^G(D)`, and `C ∈ B^G`.  So `1_T` lies in the localizing
subcategory generated by `C` and `C(G) ⊗ D` for bootstrap `D`, which is `B^G`.
`Res 1_T ≃ 0` and `1_T ∈ B^G`, so by item 5 of the splitting node `θ_(1_T) = 1`.
(The cells of the cellular approximation of `C` are `C(G)`-cells: Meyer--Nest
construction, standard, not re-read.)  ∎

**Lemma 2 (phantom transfer).**  Let `f : X → Y` be a morphism in `KK^G`
between objects with contractible restriction, with `θ_X = 1`, and let
`Z = cone(f)`.  Then `(1 − e)Y ≅ (1 − e)Z`.  In particular `Y` has zero phantom
part iff `Z` does.

*Proof.*  `e` is a natural idempotent on the full triangulated subcategory
`{E : Res E ≃ 0}` and commutes with suspension.  Splitting a triangle by a
natural idempotent gives a triangle `(1 − e)X → (1 − e)Y → (1 − e)Z`, since a
direct summand of an exact triangle is exact in an idempotent-complete
triangulated category.  `θ_X = 1` gives `e_X = 1`, so `(1 − e)X = 0`.  ∎

## 10. The equivariant diagonal of a group algebra

Let `Γ` be a countable discrete group and `D = C*_r(Γ)`.  Then
`N(D) = C*_r(Γ^p)` with `σ` permuting coordinates, and
`N(D) ⋊ G = C*_r(Γ ≀ Z/p)`.  The diagonal subgroup `ΔΓ ≤ Γ^p` is fixed
pointwise by `σ`, so the subgroup inclusion gives a `G`-equivariant
\*-homomorphism

    Δ : τ(C*_r Γ) → N(C*_r Γ),   λ_γ ↦ λ_(γ, …, γ).

This is a Tate diagonal for group algebras.  No such map exists for a general
`A`, because `a ↦ a ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ a` is not linear.  `T(Δ) : 1_T ⊗ τ(D) → T(D)` has
source with `θ = θ_(1_T) ⊗ θ_(τD) = 1`, by Lemma 1 and monoidality of `θ`.

**Corollary 3.**  The phantom part of `T(C*_r Γ)` is the phantom part of
`Z_Γ := cone(T(Δ))`.

**Lemma 4 (fixed cosets).**  The `σ`-fixed points of `Γ^p/ΔΓ` are in
bijection with `{δ ∈ Γ : δ^p = 1}`, through `δ ↦ (1, δ^(−1), …, δ^(−(p−1)))ΔΓ`.
Every other `G`-orbit is free.

*Proof.*  `σ(γ)ΔΓ = γΔΓ` iff `γ^(−1)σ(γ) = (δ, …, δ)` for some `δ`, iff
`γ_(i+1) = γ_i δ^(−1)` cyclically, which forces `δ^p = 1`.  Normalize
`γ_1 = 1` by right multiplication with `ΔΓ`: the representative is then
unique.  Orbits of a prime-order group are trivial or free.  ∎

So when `Γ` has no `p`-torsion, the trivial coset is the only fixed point.
This is the isotropy picture of the diagonal.

## 11. The adversarial test: `Γ` infinite hyperbolic with property (T)

**(a) `N(C*_r Γ)` is not itself a Meyer--Nadareishvili test object.**
`MN(all separable)` needs `Res A ∈ B` and `A ⋊ G ∈ B`.  `Res N(D) = C*_r(Γ^p)`
is a reduced algebra of an infinite Kazhdan group.  Skandalis's
non-K-nuclearity mechanism (recorded in
`research/artifacts/stw-uct-reduction-map-2026-09-11.md`, §4) is expected to put
it outside `B`.  That was not re-derived for `Γ^p`.  The right test object is
`T(D)`: its restriction is contractible, and by Corollary 3 its phantom part is
that of `Z_Γ`.

**(b) Crossed products.**  `(1_T ⊗ τD) ⋊ G = (1_T ⋊ G) ⊗ C*_r Γ = 1_T ⋊_r (Γ × G)`,
with `Γ` acting trivially on `1_T`.  `T(D) ⋊ G = 1_T ⋊_r (Γ ≀ G)`, with `Γ^p`
acting trivially.  `T(Δ) ⋊ G` is the subgroup inclusion
`ΔΓ × G ≤ Γ ≀ G`, and `ΔΓ × G` is the centralizer of `σ`.

**(c) Every K-theoretic test passes (sketch, cellular step not fully checked).**
Let `Γ` be torsion-free and hyperbolic, for instance a torsion-free uniform
lattice in `Sp(n,1)`, `n ≥ 2`.
- Baum--Connes with coefficients holds for `Γ ≀ G`
  (`hyperbolic-bcc-finite-wreath-products`) and for `Γ × G`.
- Finite subgroups of `Γ ≀ G` are trivial or conjugate to `<σ>`, because
  `H^1(G; Coind_1^G Γ) = H^1(1; Γ) = 1` (Shapiro).
- With coefficients `1_T ⊗ B`, cells of `E(Γ ≀ G)` with trivial isotropy
  contribute `K_*(Res 1_T ⊗ B) = 0`.
- The left side therefore localizes onto the `<σ>`-singular part,
  `(Γ ≀ G) ×_(ΔΓ × G) E(Γ ≀ G)^σ`, with `E(Γ ≀ G)^σ` a model for `EΓ`.  That is the left side for
  `ΔΓ × G`.
So `T(Δ) ⋊ G` induces isomorphisms on `K_*(− ⊗ B)` for every separable `B`,
`Res Z_Γ ≃ 0`, and `Z_Γ ⋊ G` is K-invisible with all trivial-action
coefficients.

**(d) Amenable-type calibration.**  If `Γ` is torsion-free and a-T-menable,
then `C*_r Γ ∈ B`.  So `T(D) ∈ B^G` (part 2, §7 item 2), and `Z_Γ ∈ B^G` has
contractible restriction and a K-invisible crossed product, so `Z_Γ ≃ 0`.  The
Tate diagonal is then a `KK^G`-equivalence, and `T(C*_r Γ)` has no phantom
part.  This is the case that tells us nothing.

**(e) Where it dies for Kazhdan `Γ`.**  Descend the `γ`-elements of `Γ × G` and
`Γ ≀ G`.  The Kasparov--Skandalis `γ` exists for these bolic actions (standard,
not re-read).
- On the `γ`-parts, `T(Δ) ⋊ G` is a K-isomorphism between objects of the
  cellular class, hence a KK-equivalence.
- `Z_Γ ⋊ G` is therefore equivalent to the cone of the induced map between
  the `(1 − γ)`-parts.  Those parts vanish when `γ = 1` and are nonzero-type
  objects when `Γ` has (T), by Skandalis.  They are invisible to K-theory with
  every trivial-action coefficient.
- Detection for `Z_Γ` needs `Z_Γ ⋊ G ≃_KK 0`.  A phantom needs `θ_(Z_Γ) ≠ 1`.
  Both are statements about KK-morphisms between `(1 − γ)`-parts.  No
  available invariant sees them: K-theory with coefficients fails by (c), and
  Köhler invariants fail by `bootstrap-zp-actions-realize-every-cyclotomic-k-module`.

**Verdict.**  Unreviewed.  The permutation action on `C*_r(Γ^p)` passes every
K-theoretic test, and its Tate part reduces exactly to the `(1 − γ)`-part of
the Tate diagonal.  It gives a counterexample to `MN(all separable)` iff the
shift on the Tate part of that non-K-nuclear summand is not `KK^G`-trivial.
That is posed as the open claim `tate-norm-shift-is-kkg-trivial`, item 2.  No
phantom was produced, and none was excluded.

**Sharpest sub-question.**  Is `T(Δ)` a `KK^G`-equivalence for a torsion-free
Kazhdan hyperbolic `Γ`?  A positive answer shows these permutation actions give
no separable counterexample.  A negative answer, together with
`Z_Γ ⋊ G ≃_KK 0`, would refute `MN(all separable)`.
